comments.content: Dead fail policy: Policy.fail and Route 'reject' are never read/returned by routeOf(). Claimed fail-open/fail-closed behavior is unenforced; low-signal/undefined answers silently map to noop. Branch on p.fail for error/undefined paths or remove the field.

Worker never calls Queue.fail and ignores runPool errors: runPool swallows worker exceptions into {ok,errors} (src/pools/pool.ts), so a throwing opts.work leaves the row in 'running' forever, stats.failed stays 0, and resume will loop. Wrap work in try/catch and call q.fail on error, and handle runPool errors.

DB handle leaks on error path: db.close() is only reached on happy path. If DUP check throws (or future work throws out of loop), WAL handle/lock is leaked, hurting crash-recovery. Use try/finally for db.close().

Budget/stopAfter accounting races under concurrency: `processed` is checked then incremented across concurrent runPool lanes, and `room` is computed from stats().done per batch without counting in-flight claims. This can overshoot budgetCalls HARD CAP and distorts resumed/processed metrics.
comments.existing_code:
const room = opts.budgetCalls !== undefined ? Math.max(0, opts.budgetCalls - doneNow) : Infinity;
    const batch = q.claim(Math.min(opts.concurrency ?? 4, 16, room));

comments.content: Check-then-act TOCTOU: `roomLeft()` is checked before `await judge.ask()`, then `spend()` after. With `runPool` concurrency 6 (decision-tree/find/filter), N lanes can all pass `roomLeft()` before any `spend()` runs, overshooting calls/usd caps. The spend already happened (cost incurred) and `spend()` throw is swallowed into noop/errors. Make budget reservation atomic (e.g. `tryReserve():boolean` that increments synchronously before the async call, rollback on failure) or serialize the budgeted section.

Caps object aliased: constructor stores `caps` by reference and `used()` returns `caps: this.caps` directly. Any holder of the original object or the returned object can mutate limits and silently disable the hard stop. Defensive-copy on both ends.
